The corpus contains numerous allegations against Jeffrey Epstein concerning his conduct toward minors, spanning criminal charges, civil complaints, and litigation filings:

1. Federal sex-trafficking charges (2019 SDNY indictment): A federal grand jury in the Southern District of New York returned a sealed indictment on July 2, 2019 charging Epstein with one count of sex trafficking of minors (18 U.S.C. § 1591) and one count of conspiracy to commit sex trafficking of minors. The indictment alleges that over many years Epstein "sexually exploited and abused dozens of minor girls" at his homes in Manhattan, New York, and Palm Beach, Florida. From at least 2002 through at least 2005, he allegedly enticed and recruited (or caused to be recruited) minor girls to visit his residences to engage in sex acts, after which he gave victims hundreds of dollars in cash. He also allegedly paid certain victims to recruit additional girls, creating a "vast network of underage victims," some as young as 14 years old and often particularly vulnerable to exploitation (EFTA00028990, EFTA02731082, EFTA00028467).

2. Palm Beach state case / plea (2008): Police in Palm Beach, Florida began investigating Epstein in 2005 after a parent complained that he had sexually abused her 14-year-old daughter. Epstein pleaded guilty and was convicted in 2008 in Florida state court of procuring a child for prostitution and soliciting a prostitute, serving almost 13 months with extensive work release. Federal officials had identified numerous victims, some as young as 14, whom Epstein had allegedly sexually abused (EFTA00263107, EFTA00263435, EFTA01661603).

3. Statement of Undisputed Facts (Epstein v. Rothstein/Edwards, Palm Beach County): This filing alleges that Epstein "has a sexual preference for young children" and that he "repeatedly sexually assaulted more than forty (40) young girls" on numerous occasions. It notes that when questioned on the subject at his March 17, 2010 deposition, Epstein invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination (EFTA00729910, EFTA00725998, EFTA01100638, EFTA00081180).

4. Civil trafficking litigation: Complaints (e.g., Jane Doe 1 v. JPMorgan Chase and the U.S. Virgin Islands actions) describe Epstein operating a "widespread and well-publicized sex-trafficking operation" / "international sex-trafficking organization" and bring claims under the federal anti-sex-trafficking statute (TVPA, 18 U.S.C. § 1591 et seq.) related to the sexual abuse of victims (EFTA00162121, EFTA00145666, EFTA00161836, EFTA00104216).

Note: The 2019 federal indictment against Epstein was vacated following his death in August 2019 (EFTA00028467). These are allegations and, in the Palm Beach state case, convictions on the two counts to which he pleaded guilty.
